correctness.rationale: The projection kernel is exactly \(2^{-n}\) times an integer character sum; character-orthogonality and translation averaging establish the sharp and minimal endpoint norm. A cubic root-of-unity filter gives the closed kernel at every Hamming weight. Binomial even/odd sum identities yield both formulas; 3B_n-A_n=2A_{n-1} establishes strict uniqueness for all n≥3. Independent exact-integer methods verify n=3..18 and boundary inequalities through n=100.

value.rationale: For all n≥3 the three Fourier subspace ranks differ by at most one but the corresponding sharp projection norms have exactly two distinct levels, a unique minimizing residue, and an exponentially increasing gap with nontrivial constant limiting ratio. Exact endpoint conditioning for nearly equal-dimensional modular Walsh spaces is a natural stable-projection optimization question, not just a finite census.
